lead: Murders dipped 3.5% in the latest quarter but about 60 people are still killed daily, while the rand hit its weakest level of 2026 as Gauteng and eThekwini coalition talks drag on ahead of next week's council deadlines.

items.title: Murders down 3.5% in July-September, but 60 people still killed a day
items.summary: Acting police minister Firoz Cachalia reported 5,590 murders for the quarter, 204 fewer than a year earlier. Carjackings fell sharply, but kidnappings, attempted murders and cash-in-transit heists rose. Gauteng recorded the most murders.

items.title: FF Plus bid to unite DA and ActionSA in Gauteng metros fails
items.summary: Talks stalled over mayoral candidates, with ActionSA wanting Helen Zille and Cilliers Brink replaced. An ANC-led framework would give ActionSA Joburg and Tshwane; councils have been urged to sit by 27 November.

items.title: ANC KZN figure accused of lobbying against an MK deal in eThekwini
items.summary: Unnamed sources say a senior ANC provincial task team member met Durban business people to push an ANC-DA-IFP alternative. ANC KZN says it wants a stable, signed coalition, with an outcome expected within 48 hours. MK holds 86 of 221 seats.

items.title: KZN launches festive-season crime crackdown across 184 police stations
items.summary: Premier Thamsanqa Ntuli and acting provincial commissioner Phumelele Makoba unveiled a phased plan running to late January, covering matric exams, beaches, roads and school reopening. Ntuli warned crime threatens R124bn in investment pledges.

items.title: Share of KZN homes with long water outages has more than doubled
items.summary: Stats SA's household survey found 44.7% of KwaZulu-Natal households had prolonged water interruptions in 2025, up from 21.6% in 2012 and above the 37.6% national figure.

items.title: One dead, about 11 hurt in Phoenix shootout
items.summary: Two groups allegedly exchanged rifle fire on Lenham Drive in Phoenix, north of Durban, on Thursday night after an earlier clash and a road collision. Bystanders were among the injured; no arrests were reported.

items.title: Continental weighs closing Gqeberha tyre plant, 950 jobs at risk
items.summary: The company cited spare capacity and cheap imports and has opened formal retrenchment consultations. The motor industry body urged it to exhaust alternatives, pointing to Eastern Cape unemployment of 44.3%.

items.title: Severe thunderstorm warning for KZN and six other provinces today
items.summary: The weather service has a yellow level 2 warning for heavy rain, hail and damaging winds, with possible localised flooding. Eastern KZN faces hot, humid conditions and a very high UV index.

items.title: Russian strikes damage Kyiv bridges, killing eight
items.summary: Ballistic missiles hit three Dnipro bridges and cut power in several regions after Putin promised retaliation over damage to the Kerch Bridge. Moscow said the bridges carried military equipment.

items.title: Poland says Russian missiles and drone entered its airspace
items.summary: Warsaw called three overnight incursions a deliberate provocation and will seek more NATO support on its eastern flank. NATO chief Mark Rutte is due in Warsaw today.

items.title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
items.summary: The court found against Myanmar by nine votes to six and ordered compensation and safe return of displaced Rohingya. Myanmar and China rejected the ruling as unfair.

items.title: UK and EU agree trade, carbon and youth mobility deals
items.summary: A Brussels summit produced agreements to ease food checks, link carbon markets and let up to 100,000 young people a year live on each side. Tuition fees and car rules remain unresolved.

items.title: Trump defends Putin ties and accuses Iran of stalling
items.summary: Back from Asia, Trump said Putin wants a diplomatic end to the Ukraine war and that Tehran is not negotiating honestly. He also said a trade deal with Mexico is close.

items.title: Malawi fuel crisis brings rationing and long queues
items.summary: Motorists face daily limits of about 20 litres and violence at filling stations, while black-market fuel has caused deadly explosions. Officials blame forex and logistics problems.

items.title: Rand slides to weakest level of 2026 near R17.54/$
items.summary: The currency fell further on Friday, pressured by a firm dollar and uncertainty over who will govern Gauteng's metros. It is down about 4.4% this month.

items.title: JSE at lowest close in over a year after two bruising sessions
items.summary: The All Share ended Thursday 0.33% lower at 106,216 after a 3.66% slump on Wednesday. Bond yields jumped and gold fell; Investec says an S&P upgrade could come soon.

items.title: SARB holds repo at 7.25% in a split 4-3 vote
items.summary: Three MPC members wanted a hike as October inflation reached 5.2%, driven by fuel. Prime stays at 10.75%, and unions called for relief for households.

items.title: Springboks face Ireland in Dublin in must-win Test today
items.summary: Eben Etzebeth returns in one of five changes after last week's 21-19 loss to France. The Boks sit a point behind the All Blacks, and need a win to reach the Nations Championship final in London.

items.title: Proteas crush Bangladesh by nine wickets; Bavuma out of 2nd Test
items.summary: Simon Harmer took six wickets and Kagiso Rabada was player of the match at the Wanderers, putting SA 1-0 up and top of the WTC table. Markram will captain at SuperSport Park from Monday.

items.title: Pirates meet Stellenbosch in Carling Knockout semi in Durban
items.summary: The semi-final has been moved to Moses Mabhida Stadium for a 3.30pm kick-off today, and Stellenbosch's Hunt says his side can pull off an upset.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
items.summary: Levent Alpöge says he and Claude produced a formal proof of the famous conjecture, posted in the Lean proof language. Mathematicians are still checking it, and a separate human proof claim emerged the same day.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models
items.summary: Astra targets demanding work such as coding and research, while Sol is for everyday tasks and agents. According to the system card, both reached OpenAI's critical threshold for cybersecurity risk.
